bug_semantics: Authenticated SQL injection (CWE-89) in packages/Webkul/Admin/src/DataGrids/Lead/LeadDataGrid.php: prepareQueryBuilder() concatenates the user-controlled rotten_lead[in] query parameter (Laravel request()->input('rotten_lead.in')) into Laravel havingRaw() with no placeholder binding or integer cast. Because rotten_lead is a computed CASE/DATEDIFF alias, the filter is applied in HAVING after GROUP BY leads.id. An authenticated user with leads access can GET /admin/leads?rotten_lead[in]=99+OR+SLEEP(5) (time-based) or 99+OR+1=1 (boolean) and extract the full database, including credential hashes. Independently confirmed on commit ba25b7e7 (still concatenated) and patched in v2.2.4.
flaw_origin: The sink was created as a feature, not a later botch of a safe filter. On 2022-08-31 commit f344238f734bcba261a885870ba9d205fb8aeccf ('added rotten lead filter') first added the computed rotten_lead select alias and the filter if (! is_null(request()->input('rotten_lead.in'))) { $queryBuilder->havingRaw('rotten_lead = ' . request()->input('rotten_lead.in')); } in LeadDataGrid.php (lines 142-144 at that commit). Subsequent commits only added a table-prefix prefix and Pint formatting; they preserved string concatenation of the request value. The first-write therefore is the BIC.
